content.abstract:
iii
EXPEDITION - AN OVERVIEW
KR Sivan, Leader, XVII Indian Expedition to Antarctica 
In the Golden Jubilee Year of Indian Independence, India launched
the XVII Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica in continuation for the
quest of science. The expedition vessel MV Polar Bird with 49 members ! 
on board sailed off from Murmugao Port, Goa on Monday, the 08th
December 1997 at 1900 hours. The composition of the team consists of
Scientists from 17 Organisations/Academic Institution, 13 members Logistic
Team from Indian Army, DOD Observer and cooks from ITBP. Later the
strength became 53 when the Medical Officer of the expedition and three
German Scientists joined at Mauritius.
It was the first time that the launching ceremony was held at the
newly constructed Antarctic Study Centre (now NCAOR), Goa and ASC/
DOD made it a grand occasion. Hon. Dy. Chief Minister of Goa,
Dr. Wilfred D'Souza and dignitaries, families and friends gathered in large
numbers and bid Bon-Voyage with blessings and good wishes.
Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica is a challenging,
adventurous and a national commitment for the quest of science. Unknown
are many but to face it and overcome, proper planning and dedicated team
spirit to tackle the situation is very much essential. During the cruise itself,
the members had shown their high team spirit. They had to face severe
problem on board ship, from the day one of the sailing, when some of the
system failed and had to face lot of inconvenience. Added to this, there was
no Medical Officer accompanied the team from Goa. But the members never
got panicky but always behaved like true expeditioners.
We had halted at Mauritius from 16 to 19th Dec 97. It was a great
relief for the members that after a weeklong journey on  board ship, they
could see some mankind and also the beauty of Mauritius. Added to this
was the witnessing of shooting of one of Hindi films in the beaches of
Mauritius casting Indian favorite stars Govinda and Karishma Kapoor.
The Medical Officer for the expedition, thre e Scientists from
Institute of Planetary Geodesy Germany and two Jayrow helicopters with the
crewmembers were joined at Mauritius.
iv
Indian High Commissioner Mr. Mani Tripati, Ms. R uchira Patni,
First Secretary and staff accorded us warm reception and all the help required
were provided during onward journey and return journey. We are thankful
for them for all the help and for fabulous luncheon given to the members.
We were also honored and felt happy when Hon.Dy. Prime Minister, Mr,
Kailash Purryag and Minister for Telecommunication & Information, Mr.
Sarat Dutt Lallah of Mauritius accompanied by Indian High Commissioner
paid visits to our expedition vessel and they had shown keen interest in the
Antarctic Scientific Programme..
The period of stay at Mauritius was also utilised by the ship to rectify
the defects and put the system in order. On completion of the repairs, further
voyage started on 20th Dec 97. The voyage time was fully utilized by
organising project presentation by the participants, various games and
tournaments etc and all the members enthusiastically participated in all the
activities. This helped to avoid the long monotonous ship journey and
seasickness. These also helped in understanding the expedition programme
and priority wise plan the summer tasks
For the success of any expedition, logistic support is the backbone
and the backup from the parent organisation of the participants. I am happy
to record here that the Logistic Team from the Indian Army lead by Major
G Narayan and ably supported by Capt KS Panesar may be the best so far
came to Antarctica in all respects. Their untiring efforts, motivation and high
team spirit shown that nothing is impossible in the harsh place like Antarctica.
The assistance and the rescue operation carried out by the team during the
polar night period when the 43rd Russian Expedition Team met with the
unfortunate MI8 helicopter crash on ice shelf and the rescue of four convoy
team members stranded on blue ice are note worthy and an example for
others.
Our summer programme started with a jolt when the s cientific
equipment and instruments while carrying by underslung crash-landed on
pack ice on 06th and 08th January 98 due to technical snag of the helicopter.
But the state of mind of all the members given me the required courage to
face the situation and they lend their invaluable support to carry on with
the activities. I am happy to say that all the Scientific and Logistic program
assigned for the summer period had been successfully completed inspite of
the initial set back. We owe our gratitude to the heads of organisations who
had given us all the support and guidance not only during the crisis but also
through out the period of expedition.
